summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type II diabetes, hypertension, and depression, was admitted for severe hyperglycemia with a blood glucose of 754 mg/dL after missing her morning NPH insulin and consuming sweetened tea. She did not have diabetic ketoacidosis. Her insulin regimen was changed from NPH to glargine 32 units at bedtime with a humalog sliding scale due to poor glycemic control and prior hypoglycemia. She received nutrition counseling and education on insulin pen use. Her creatinine improved from 1.5 to 1.1 mg/dL, likely due to resolution of prerenal acute kidney injury, and she has follow-up scheduled with nephrology. Skin abscesses from a prior admission were monitored, remained clean without infection, and continued on outpatient wound care. She was discharged home with home health services, new insulin therapy, and follow-up arranged for diabetes, surgery, and kidney function.
